scope: Repair booking venture revision 3; moving from homeowners to maintenance teams.
goal: Establish a recurring paid coordination job for small property maintenance teams.
current_question: Does the old homeowner landing-page result justify proceeding with the current business-customer pilot?

branch_criteria.continue: Evidence from the current maintenance-team customer and job meets a newly frozen pilot condition.
branch_criteria.narrow: One reachable maintenance-team subgroup has a verified repeated coordination failure.
branch_criteria.stop: Current target users report no material unmet job after the agreed inquiry.
branch_criteria.unknown: Evidence concerns an earlier scope or insufficient current target users; rewrite the scoped test.

selection.limitation: Unlinked relevant facts may be omitted. Selection is not semantic retrieval.

records.text: Scope revision 1 targeted individual homeowners. Twelve of forty visitors clicked a hypothetical 9 euro booking button; there were no payments.
The old test's frozen criterion was ten clicks before prototyping for homeowners. The click threshold was reached, but it was never a business-customer criterion.
A later decision changed scope to revision 3: maintenance teams coordinating repeat repairs across properties. It explicitly supersedes the homeowner prototype objective.
One maintenance manager describes spreadsheet coordination; no measured delay, buying authority, paid commitment or repeated observation exists.
An outstanding research submission was produced against scope revision 1. A separate current-scope accessibility audit remains active and does not depend on the homeowner test.
